title: Hydropower hit record lows in the US Southwest this summer
gist: A 27-year Colorado River drought cut US Southwest hydropower 28% below its 10-year average in Apr–Aug 2026, leaving Lake Powell <1% above Glen Canyon's minimum power pool and Lake Mead 9% above Hoover's; EIA sees US hydro output at a 10+ year low in 2026 and lower in 2027, and the IEA links hydro shortfalls to rising emissions.

insights.claim: US Southwest hydropower generation between April and August 2026 was 28% below the 10-year average, per US Energy Information Administration data.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Regional baseload/dispatchable hydro shortfall must be filled by gas or other sources, supporting Southwest power prices and gas burn.
insights.quote: The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average

insights.claim: At end-September 2026 Lake Powell stood at 3,518 feet, less than 1% above the minimum level needed to run water through the Glen Canyon power plant turbines.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Glen Canyon is at risk of hitting minimum power pool, which would halt generation outright — a binary risk for Western grid supply.
insights.quote: less than 1% above the level required to run the water through turbines
insights.locator: At the end of September, Lake Powell

insights.claim: The Hoover Dam power plant needs Lake Mead at 950 feet to generate, and the reservoir was only 9% above that minimum in September 2026.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Hoover has a thin buffer; further drawdown threatens a second major Southwest hydro asset.
insights.locator: The Hoover Dam power plant requires 950 feet

insights.claim: Glen Canyon and Hoover Dam together produced nearly 7 TWh of electricity in 2025, enough to serve over 2 million people.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Sizes the replacement-power need if these plants fall below minimum pool — material for Southwest utilities and power marketers.
insights.locator: Together, the two plants produced nearly seven terawatt-hours

insights.claim: Rocky Mountain snowfall supplies about 85% of the Colorado River's annual flow, and the river has recently seen record-low flows amid a 27-year regional drought.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Snowpack readings are the leading indicator for Southwest hydro output and water allocations; watch them each winter/spring.
insights.quote: Snowfall in the Rocky Mountains provides about 85% of the annual flow of the Colorado River
insights.locator: Residents and farmers in the US Southwest

insights.claim: Climate change undermines hydropower reliability via more droughts, warmer winters with less snow and ice to fill reservoirs, and more variable precipitation causing alternating floods and droughts, though some regions globally will get wetter.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Hydro should be treated as an increasingly volatile, not firm, resource in long-term grid and utility models; effects are regionally uneven.
insights.quote: more variability in precipitation can lead to alternating floods and droughts, making the power source less reliable
insights.locator: The effects of climate change on hydropower

themes.theme: Outlook: EIA projections and El Nino

insights.claim: The EIA projects US hydropower production in 2026 will likely be its lowest in over a decade, falling even lower in 2027.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Multi-year hydro deficit implies sustained demand for replacement generation (gas, solar+storage) and tighter Western power markets into 2027.
insights.quote: Hydropower production is likely to be at its lowest level in over a decade in 2026 and tick even lower in 2027
insights.locator: Hydropower production is likely to be

insights.claim: October–November 2026 El Nino-linked heavy rains raised Lake Powell more than 20 feet from its mid-September low, but this is only temporary relief against decades of drought.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Don't over-read short-term reservoir bounces; structural recovery needs far more inflow, so the hydro deficit thesis stays intact.
insights.quote: it’ll take much more to help reservoirs recover from decades of drought conditions
insights.locator: El Niño could provide some temporary relief

insights.claim: A worldwide hydropower generation shortfall accounted for about 40% of the 1.1% rise in global energy-related greenhouse-gas emissions in 2023, per the International Energy Agency.
insights.speaker: Casey Crownhart
insights.so_what: Hydro droughts force fossil backfill, lifting emissions and fossil fuel demand — a hidden driver of gas/coal burn and carbon prices.
insights.quote: A worldwide shortfall in hydropower generation accounted for about 40% of that rise
